pr.title: Leave a cancelled run's checks out of CHECKS and the panel's checks, and note a draft a hold shadows
pr.head: d98ba51aadde13079a43cd4c240e59979f3a78dc

summary: Projector reads a pull request's CI results in two places. The watch daemon is a background process that polls each pull request a session subscribes to. When a check fails, it sends a CHECKS event to the session that fixes the pull request. The panel is the list of pull requests Projector draws in Claude Code. It colors a failing row failing, and the row's drawer reads checks failing. Both read GitHub's check rollup: every check run and commit status on the head commit, with counts by state.

Some repositories start CI on GitHub's labeled event and cancel a pull request's earlier run when a new one starts (concurrency: cancel-in-progress). A review adds the reviewing label when it starts, so each review cancels the run in progress. GitHub keeps the cancelled run's checks on the head beside the newer run's. A gathering job, one that runs if: always() once the jobs it needs end, then fails in the cancelled run. So the daemon and the panel reported a failure that no code caused.

This change tells a cancelled run's two kinds of failure apart. The cancel time is the earliest end of the run's check runs that concluded CANCELLED. Each failure is then handled by when it started:
  • A check that started at or after the cancel is a gathering job that failed because of the cancel. It is always left out.
  • A check that started before the cancel failed on its own. It is left out only once a newer run of the same workflow is still running or has run a check of the same name without skipping it.

A head with nothing failing or pending, whose every workflow's newest run was cancelled, reads checks cancelled. The panel also notes cancelled on a row while a workflow's newest run on the head was cancelled, and notes draft when another status takes a draft's word. docs/cli.md gains a section on keeping review labels from cancelling CI runs.

cards.title: Review history so far
cards.html:
• 829877f: changes requested. The first version dropped every failure in a cancelled run, which hid a check that failed before the cancel. It also counted a job that passed before the cancel as passing, so a head whose only run was cancelled could read checks passing.
  • d98ba51: clean. Both findings are fixed and settled. One suggestion remains: rewrap a line of docs/plugins.md and a line of the checksOf comment.

groups.title: The daemon leaves out the failures a cancel caused or a newer run retested
groups.kicker: How the watch daemon decides which failed checks to report
intro: The daemon's query now asks for each check run's start and end, its suite (workflow run) conclusion, and the workflow run's id, workflow, and start. failures keeps the old rule for what counts as a failure. failed_contexts, which names the checks in a CHECKS event, then drops a failure when caused_by_cancel or superseded says so.

cancel_times finds when each cancelled run was cancelled, as the earliest end of its check runs that concluded CANCELLED. caused_by_cancel is true for a failure that started at or after that time. superseded is true when a newer run of the same workflow is still running, or ran a check of the same name that neither skipped nor was cancelled. When no cancelled check run of the run was read, the cancel time is unknown, and the failure counts.

checks.text: With hand-built rollups against this head: a lint that failed before the cancel, next to a label run that skipped every job, gives ['lint']; a gathering job that failed after the cancel gives [], whether the newer run passed or skipped every job. The panel's checksOf gives failing, passing, and passing for the same rollups.

files.note: Adds run_id, cancel_times, caused_by_cancel, workflow_run, and superseded, and widens the rollup query.

checks.text: The paging loop counts every failure, cancelled-run ones included, so the nodes the daemon writes to its cache hold every failure the counts hold. The panel reads those cached nodes, so it reaches the same answer as the daemon. Checked by reading read_contexts and the paging test.

files.note: Tables of cases for a failure the cancel caused and for one a newer run retests, and a test that a check failed before its run was cancelled is still a CI failure.

groups.title: The panel applies the same rules to its checks
groups.kicker: How the panel turns the rollup into one checks state
intro: checksOf now always counts by state and takes out the projector/review status. It then moves each failed check run that causedByCancel or supersededOf picks out from failing to cancelled. These are the same rules the daemon uses. The state is failing or pending when those have a count. Otherwise the state is cancelled when every workflow's newest run on the head was cancelled, and passing after that.

cancelledOf sets isCancelled when some workflow's newest run on the head was cancelled, using newestRuns. The panel's own query, used for pull requests the daemon has no result for, reads the first 20 contexts with the same fields as the daemon's.

files.note: Adds runOf, cancelTimesOf, causedByCancel, supersededOf, and newestRuns, and rewrites checksOf to count every time.

checks.text: A head whose only run passed one job and then was cancelled reads cancelled, not passing, because this check comes before the passing count. Checked with a hand-built rollup and the only a cancelled run, with a passed job case in parse.test.ts.

files.note: A table of timed rollups: nothing run since, a newer run that passed, one still running, an unknown cancel time, a check that failed before the cancel with each kind of newer run, and check runs no workflow run made.

groups.title: The panel draws the cancelled and draft notes
groups.kicker: What a row and its drawer show
intro: A row's notes, the words after its title, now end with cancelled, muted, while isCancelled holds. A draft whose word another status takes, such as conflict, also gets an italic draft note, because its italic number alone is easy to miss. The drawer's checks read checks cancelled in the muted color.

files.note: Adds the cancelled color, the optional note color and italic, and the two new notes.

Adds a pull request whose only run a label cancelled, whose gathering job failed after the cancel. It checks that the row reads ready with a muted cancelled note and that the drawer reads checks cancelled. It also checks that a conflicting draft notes draft in italic.

groups.title: Documentation
groups.kicker: The CLI guide and the panel's reference
intro: docs/cli.md gains "Keep review labels from cancelling CI runs". It explains how Projector tells a cancelled run's two kinds of failure apart and advises leaving labeled out of the checks' workflow. It also shows a separate workflow for a label that should start a fuller run. The CHECKS row of the events table and the panel's states, notes, and drawer checks in docs/plugins.md describe the new behavior.
